summary: Kaj Barr was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Poul Tuxen and Arthur Christensen, and at Göttingen under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later serving at Copenhagen from 1935 to 1945.

Kakichi Kadowaki was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from 1944 to 1947, trained under Sogen Omori, and held a post at Sophia University from approximately 1966 to 1996.
Kakushō Ujiie was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed research study at Tribhuvan University and held a professorship at Koyasan University, attested in 1970 and 1984–1985.

Kali Kinkar Datta was a historian and Indologist. He served as Honorary Director and Joint Director at the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute and as Vice-Chancellor of Patna University, attested in 1973.

Kalidas Nag was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, and under Sylvain Lévi, later holding posts at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, and The Asiatic Society.
Kalpana K. Sheth is an Indologist who completed her doctoral studies under Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani and held a post at the L.D. Institute of Indology.
Kalpana Ram works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the Australian National University between 1981 and 1989 and held a post there attested in 2026.

Kalu Rinpoche was a Tibetologist and Buddhist master. He studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Ösel Ling under teachers including Drupon Norbu Dondrup, later serving as Vajra Master at Palpung and abbot of Changchub Choeling Monastery in 1957.
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as Emeritus Professor at the University of Windsor, attested in 2002.
Kamal K. Sridhar is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She held posts at Stony Brook University, serving as director, attested in 2007, and later as Professor Emerita, attested in 2026.

Kamala Tiyavanich works in Buddhist studies and history. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, and held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.
Kamaleswar Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Brown University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.

Kameshwar Nath Mishra works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1982–2001) and was a visiting research scholar at the University of Marburg in 1993.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný. He held posts at Charles University, the Oriental Institute in Prague, and Utrecht University, with visiting roles at Chicago, Heidelberg, and Paris.

Kamla Chowdhry studied at Santiniketan, the University of the Punjab, the University of Calcutta, and Michigan State University. She held posts at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972) and Harvard University.

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of Kalidasa Sanskrit Academy, and Advisor at IGNCA.

Kammie Takahashi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama, later teaching at Muhlenberg College.
Kan Hang is a scholar of archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Su Bai and served as Dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune, later serving as Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta.
Kanchu Onoue was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as a teacher at Hikone Higashi High School, attested in 1963, and later as a professor at Eizan Gakuin, attested in 1976.
